newsitem.title: UK: UK-Norway Frigg gas talks "routine, not political".
newsitem.headline: UK-Norway Frigg gas talks "routine, not political".

text.p: Next week's talks between Norwegian and British energy officials on a long-standing dispute over North Sea gas pipelines are routine and not political, a spokeswoman for the Norwegian Energy Ministry said on Thursday.
"This is a normal contact meeting which happens fairly regularly," the spokeswoman said. "It will be at an official level, not political."

Officials will meet in Oslo on November 20 for another meeting on the so-called Frigg treaty. Until now, Britain has blocked Norway from using a pipeline from Frigg to bring gas from other fields to sell into the U.K.
Under an inter-governmental treaty signed in 1976, Norway is only allowed to deliver gas produced at Frigg or one of its satellites until Frigg is fully depleted.
But Frigg output has been falling since 1992 so Norway wants to be able to use the spare capacity on the pipeline to deliver gas from other fields.
"This is a normal contact meeting which happens fairly regularly," the spokeswoman said. "It will be at an official level, not political," she said.
